# @byo-oss/notifications (formerly better-inbox)

In-app notifications as a better-auth plugin. Notifications are rows in the app's own database (any better-auth adapter), addressed by better-auth user ids, optionally org-scoped via the better-auth organization plugin.

## Install & wire

npm install @byo-oss/notifications @better-auth/core
// requires better-auth 1.7.7+; install @better-auth/core at the same version as better-auth

// server: lib/auth.ts
import { inbox } from "@byo-oss/notifications";
export const auth = betterAuth({ plugins: [inbox()] });
// then: npx @better-auth/cli migrate  (creates the `notification` table)

// client: lib/auth-client.ts
import { inboxClient } from "@byo-oss/notifications/client";
export const authClient = createAuthClient({ plugins: [inboxClient()] });

// UI (client component)
import { InboxButton } from "@byo-oss/notifications/react";
<InboxButton client={authClient} onNavigate={(href) => router.push(href)} />
// TanStack Start/Router: onNavigate={(href) => router.navigate({ href })} with useRouter() from @tanstack/react-router; mount in __root so navigations don't remount it. See examples/tanstack-start.

## Send (server-only, never an HTTP route)

await auth.api.notify({ body: { userId, type: "comment.reply", title: "...", href: "/x", body: "...", data: {...} } });
// org fan-out (requires better-auth organization plugin); one row per member:
await auth.api.notify({ body: { organizationId, roles: ["owner","admin"], type: "billing.payment_failed", title: "..." } });
// type must not start with "notifications." (reserved for the plugin's own events): notify throws BAD_REQUEST RESERVED_NOTIFICATION_TYPE, and inbox({ routes: { "notifications.x": ... } }) throws at creation ("uses a reserved type")
// userId | organizationId | both. userId + organizationId writes one row for that member (throws USER_NOT_IN_ORGANIZATION if not a member). roles/excludeUserIds apply only to fan-out (rejected with userId). excludeUserIds skips e.g. the actor. Roles/exclusion leaving nobody returns { count: 0 }; an org with zero members throws. Fan-out capped at inbox({ maxFanout: 1000 }).

## Email if unread (optional; npm install @byo-oss/mailer @wraps.dev/email)

import { mailerChannel } from "@byo-oss/notifications/mailer";
import { wrapsMailer } from "@byo-oss/mailer/wraps";
inbox({
  appUrl: "https://app.acme.com",
  channels: { email: mailerChannel({ mailer: wrapsMailer({ from: "Acme <notify@acme.com>" /* , region, client: new WrapsEmail({...}) */ }), /* replyTo: "...", render: (ctx) => ({ subject, html, text }) */ }) }, // mailer: any Mailer from @byo-oss/mailer (wrapsMailer /wraps, sesMailer /ses for an SESv2Client, emailSdkMailer /email-sdk, memoryMailer for tests); the mailer owns the sender, so no from
  // Other providers: npm install @aws-sdk/client-sesv2 for sesMailer; npm install @opencoredev/email-sdk for emailSdkMailer (createEmailClient({ adapters, telemetry: false }); supported adapters at https://byo.dev/docs/mailer/email-sdk). wrapsEmail (@byo-oss/notifications/wraps) is deprecated in 0.11: use mailerChannel.
  routes: { "billing.payment_failed": [{ channel: "email", ifUnreadAfter: { minutes: 15 }, throttle: { hours: 24 } }], "security.new_login": [{ channel: "email", cancelIfRead: false }] }, // keyed by type; "*" fallback; no rule = in-app only; a channel at most once per type
  shouldDeliver: ({ notification, user, channel }) => true, // your own opt-out check
  // presenceWindow: 120000, maxAttempts: 5, batchSize: 100 (integer 1-1000)
});
await auth.api.processDeliveries({}); // REQUIRED from a cron (every minute): sends delayed emails and retries → { sent, skipped, retrying, failed, hasMore }
// The email is skipped if the notification is read, or seen (seenAt, set once a row is ≥50% on screen for 1s in a visible tab), unless cancelIfRead: false. throttle: at most one sent email per (user, type, channel) per window; extras skipped with detail "throttled" (best-effort across concurrent processes). Impersonated sessions (admin plugin) don't count as presence. Users with no unread-count poll within presenceWindow are "away": ifUnreadAfter emails go out right away (sendNowIfAway: false to always wait). Due-now emails send inside notify only with advanced.backgroundTasks.handler, <=25 rows and outside a transaction; otherwise on the next sweep. At-least-once; atomic claim; backoff 1m doubling to 1h; rows in notificationDelivery (status pending|sending|sent|skipped|failed, detail).
// A channel is { deliver({ notification, user, appUrl }) } that throws on failure (retries until maxAttempts) and doesn't mutate its input. throw new PermanentDeliveryError(msg) (or an error with permanent: true) to fail at once, e.g. a bad address. mailerChannel maps a PermanentMailError from the mailer to PermanentDeliveryError; any other mailer error retries, even one marked permanent: true. wrapsEmail (deprecated) does this when @wraps.dev/email rejects a missing or malformed `to` (ValidationError, field to / to[n]); throttling, network, SES and account errors retry. Bounces and suppressions come back as SES events later, not as send errors.
// Test a custom channel (vitest, ESM only): import { testChannel, deliveryContext } from "@byo-oss/notifications/testing"; testChannel(() => myChannel(fake), { failing: () => myChannel(rejecting), permanentlyFailing?: () => myChannel(bouncing) })

## Events (inbox({ onEvent }), after commit)

import { createEventBus } from "@byo-oss/core";
inbox({ onEvent: createEventBus([(event) => { /* event.type, event.userId, event.subject, event.data */ }]) });
// type                                | userId    | organizationId           | subject                                  | data
// notifications.notification.created  | recipient | the notification's, if set | { type: "notification", id }           | { notificationId, notificationType }
// notifications.delivery.failed       | recipient | the notification's, if set | { type: "notificationDelivery", id }   | { deliveryId, notificationId, notificationType, channel, attempts, reason: "permanent"|"max_attempts"|"unfinished" }
// actorId is always null. No title, body, href, data or channel error text. Exports: NOTIFICATIONS_EVENT_TYPES, NotificationsEvent, NotificationCreatedEvent, DeliveryFailedEvent, NotificationsEventType.
// After commit: outside a transaction the handler runs before notify / processDeliveries returns. Of the calls that emit events, only notify joins a caller's transaction: inside runWithTransaction (from @better-auth/core/context) its events wait for the commit and are dropped on rollback. The sweep (processDeliveries, sweepAll) never joins one: its writes commit as they happen and its delivery.failed events fire at once, even if the caller rolls back; call it outside a transaction. A plain adapter.transaction(trx => ...) isn't joined at all (writes and events happen at once); wrapping it with runWithAdapter(trx, ...) joins the writes but fires their events before the commit. Pass { onAfterCommitHookError } to your runWithTransaction so an earlier after-commit hook's throw can't skip these.
// A throwing/rejecting handler is logged ("onEvent failed for <type>") and never fails notify or the sweep.
// One event per row: an org fan-out of N awaits N handler calls (bounded by maxFanout). No ordering across events. delivery.failed can repeat for one delivery (a send outliving its 5-minute lease is retried or failed as "unfinished" while the original finishes; the same cause by which a crash after SES accepted the email can send it twice). The original send can still succeed after an "unfinished" event (row ends sent): check the row before acting.
// Adapters without transactions: events fire at once; a throw keeps rows and events. A third-party adapter whose transaction builds a new adapter object without real rollback drops events on a throw while its rows stay.
// Never route notifications.* events back into notify (loop); notify rejects them, a forwarder that renames the type isn't caught.

## @byo-oss/core hooks (byo)

// the plugin declares byo: { sweep, deleteOrganizationData, deleteMemberData }; with organizationCleanup: false only sweep
await sweepAll(auth) // from @byo-oss/core: runs the same sweep as processDeliveries; one cron route for every BYO plugin can replace the processDeliveries call
await deleteOrganizationData(auth, organizationId) // from @byo-oss/core: fan-out reaches this plugin's cleanup; running it after the plugin's own cleanup is a no-op
// a stale send with no attempts left is failed one row at a time, at most `limit` per sweep; hasMore can be true with nothing due (the sweep stopped at that cap after failing rows there), and exhausted rows past it stay "sending" until a later sweep; rows the sweep can't update still count against limit, so once limit of them (up to 180) come first, later exhausted rows wait

## Organization cleanup and export (server-only functions, not endpoints)

// automatic after /organization/delete (org's rows), /organization/remove-member and /organization/leave (that member's rows in that org); inbox({ organizationCleanup: false }) turns it off, and also leaves notifications out of @byo-oss/core's deleteOrganizationData/deleteMemberData fan-out
// deleting a user removes their notifications, deliveries and presence (FK cascade on SQL; a user-delete hook elsewhere)
await deleteOrganizationData(auth, organizationId) // → { notifications }; for deletes made any other way
await deleteMemberData(auth, { userId, organizationId }) // → { notifications }
// inside a better-auth transaction (runWithTransaction, e.g. a @better-auth/scim projection deprovisioning a member) both run in it and roll back with it
// notify inside a transaction: notification + delivery rows join it; nothing is sent inside notify; the next processDeliveries sweep (after commit) sends due emails
await exportNotificationsData(auth, { organizationId?, cursor?, limit: 500 }) // limit 1-1000; → { notifications: [{ ...row, userEmail, deliveries }], cursor }; loop until cursor is null; plain JSON, ISO dates; pages follow createdAt, so a delete mid-export doesn't skip a row; a bare-number (offset) cursor from an earlier release throws, start over with no cursor

## Read/mutate (session-scoped to caller)

auth.api.listNotifications({ headers, query: { filter: "unread"|"all", limit: 20, offset: 0, organizationId } }) → { notifications, hasMore }
auth.api.markRead({ headers, body: { id } })
auth.api.markSeen({ headers, body: { ids } }) // ≤100; cancels pending emails; InboxPanel calls it for rows actually on screen
auth.api.markAllRead({ headers, body: { organizationId? } })
auth.api.unreadCount({ headers, query: { organizationId? } }) → { count }
// same methods on the client: authClient.inbox.list / markRead / markSeen / markAllRead / unreadCount

## React hook

const { notifications, unreadCount, isLoading, hasMore, loadMore, markRead, markSeen, markAllRead, refresh, refreshIfStale } = useInbox(authClient, { pollInterval: 30000, pageSize: 20, filter: "unread"|"all", organizationId, refreshOnFocus: true });
const seenRef = useSeenOnView(markSeen, { delayMs: 1000, threshold: 0.5 }); // <li ref={n.read || n.seenAt ? undefined : seenRef(n.id)}>; IntersectionObserver, marks nothing without it
// polling refetches unread count (paused while the tab is hidden); full refresh when the tab becomes visible (refreshOnFocus, skipped if data is <5s old) and always on panel open. refresh() always fetches; refreshIfStale() respects the 5s window; concurrent refreshes share one request. markRead/markAllRead are optimistic, then refetch the unread count once the request settles (a failed refetch retries after 1s, 2s and 4s); count and list responses that started before the write can't undo it.
// filter: "unread" fetches unread rows only, so pageSize is the count you actually get. Locally-read rows stay until refresh(); loadMore() offsets by unread rows held. Changing filter refetches. InboxButton takes the same filter prop and hides its all/unread tabs when set to "unread".
// labels={{ notifications, unread, all, markAllRead, empty, loadMore, unreadCount: (n) => string, badge: (n) => string, relativeTime: (date) => string }} on InboxButton/InboxPanel; defaults in defaultInboxLabels. A polite aria-live region next to the bell announces unreadCount.
// InboxButton opens on the "unread" tab (server-filtered), tabs ordered unread, all. InboxPanel accepts view/onViewChange; uncontrolled it defaults to "unread".

## Notes

- 0.11: new `@byo-oss/notifications/mailer` entry, `mailerChannel({ mailer, replyTo?, render? })`, sends through any `Mailer` from `@byo-oss/mailer` (install it in the app, 0.1.1 or later); no `from` option. `wrapsEmail` is deprecated, unchanged, and will be removed in a later breaking release: `wrapsEmail({ from })` becomes `mailerChannel({ mailer: wrapsMailer({ from }) })`. wrapsMailer differs from wrapsEmail: it fails permanently on any @wraps.dev/email ValidationError (bad from, replyTo, recipient or empty subject) and on SES MessageRejected and InvalidParameterValue, where wrapsEmail failed only a bad recipient at once and retried the rest; it throws a TypeError at creation if from is empty; its client must resolve { messageId }; it RFC 2047-encodes a non-ASCII display name in from (mailer 0.1.1+). No schema change, no new options
- 0.10: better-auth peer ^1.7.7 and a new required peer @better-auth/core (same version); notify rejects notifications.* types and inbox({ routes }) throws at creation for a notifications.* key; onEvent and byo hooks are new; stale sends with no attempts left are failed at most `limit` per sweep (hasMore can be true with nothing due, when the sweep stopped at the cap after failing rows there; rows past the cap stay "sending" until a later sweep); inbox() throws unless batchSize is an integer from 1 to 1000; no migration
- notification fields: id, userId, organizationId?, type, title, body?, href?, data? (json), read (boolean), seenAt?, createdAt
- 0.8: every reference has onDelete: "cascade" (regenerate drizzle/prisma migrations); org delete/remove/leave cleans up automatically; tab text is "Unread"/"All"
- schema is documented in the README (Schema); uninstall: drop notificationDelivery, then inboxPresence and notification
- 0.6 adds seenAt plus tables notificationDelivery and inboxPresence: re-run migrate after upgrading
- 0.6 InboxFetchClient requires inbox.markSeen; a hand-built adapter must pass it or seen never cancels emails
- components styled with shadcn CSS variables (bg-popover, text-muted-foreground, ...); zero runtime deps; shadcn not required
- Tailwind v4: add `@source "<path>/node_modules/@byo-oss/notifications/dist";` to your CSS (v4 skips node_modules)
- InboxButton renders its own <button>; don't wrap it in one. className styles the wrapper; buttonClassName replaces the trigger's default classes (e.g. shadcn buttonVariants({ variant: "ghost", size: "icon" }))
- recommend manual index on notification (userId, createdAt); with email routes also notificationDelivery (status, scheduledFor), and with throttle (userId, type, channel, sentAt); for org cleanup/export notification (organizationId, createdAt) and notificationDelivery (notificationId); for export without organizationId, notification (createdAt)
- in lists are chunked at 90 values, so Cloudflare D1's 100-parameter limit holds
- community plugin, not affiliated with better-auth
